module.title: Unit 3: Cultural Traditions vs. Modern Lifestyles
module.objective: Mampu membandingkan tradisi lokal dan gaya hidup urban kontemporer menggunakan past habits (used to vs. would).

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Old Traditions and Modern City Life
subModules.grammarFocus: Past habits with used to and would
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Traditions, heritage, and contemporary urban life

content.summary: In this reading mission, you will explore how daily life has changed across generations. You will read about families moving from quiet countryside villages to busy cities, and how their customs either survived or changed. Along the way, you will learn how writers use 'used to' and 'would' to describe past habits and past states.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Past habits and states with 'used to' and repeated past actions with 'would'
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: cultural heritage, pass down, contemporary, ritual, urbanisation, fade away, preserve, custom, ancestor
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning for time markers and contrast words to compare past traditions with modern routines

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea and key details in texts contrasting past traditions with modern lifestyles.
Distinguish between past states and repeated past actions using 'used to' and 'would'.
Identify how contemporary urbanisation influences cultural customs over time.

contextWarmup.prompt: How did many families spend their evenings before television and smartphones became popular?
options: They would sit together and share stories or play acoustic instruments.
They used to buy groceries online every single evening.
They would stream movies on modern digital tablets.
contextWarmup.explanation: Before modern screen technology, people often gathered in person to share oral stories and play music together.

rules: Rule 1: Use 'used to + base verb' for past habits, repeated actions, or past states that are no longer true today.
Rule 2: Use 'would + base verb' only for repeated past actions or routines. Do not use 'would' with state verbs such as be, have, live, or know.
Rule 3: In negative sentences and questions, use 'did not use to' and 'did you use to' without the final letter 'd'.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use 'would' for past states like living somewhere or possessing something. However, 'would' only works for actions. For states, you must use 'used to'.
commonTrap.wrong: My grandparents would live in a wooden house near the river.
commonTrap.correct: My grandparents used to live in a wooden house near the river.

content.contractionsSubtitle: Notice how subject pronouns blend with 'would' in descriptive stories:

contractions.exampleFull: We would visit our village every summer.
contractions.exampleContracted: We'd visit our village every summer.

contractions.subject: They
contractions.exampleFull: They would bake bread together in the morning.
contractions.exampleContracted: They'd bake bread together in the morning.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Past Habits
grammarFormulas.description: Construct sentences describing past routines and states using these blocks:

complements.text: in the central square every evening

items.exampleSentence: Communities try hard to protect their cultural heritage from disappearing.
items.collocation: preserve cultural heritage / rich cultural heritage

items.exampleSentence: Elders pass down folk tales to young children during winter evenings.
items.collocation: pass down traditions / pass down recipes

items.exampleSentence: Contemporary city life offers many conveniences that our ancestors did not have.
The morning tea ritual brings the whole family together before work.
Rapid urbanisation has turned quiet green farmland into crowded apartment blocks.
Without written records, local languages can easily fade away.
items.collocation: slowly fade away / fade away over time

items.exampleSentence: The town council works to preserve ancient buildings and local crafts.
It is an old custom to take off your shoes before entering someone's home.
Our ancestors used natural stars to navigate ships across wide oceans.

paragraphs: Fifty years ago, Oakridge was a quiet farming valley where everyone knew their neighbours. Families used to live in large stone houses with three generations under one roof. Life was slow, and people followed strict seasonal routines. In the summer evenings, villagers would gather around the fountain to sing traditional folk songs, and elders would pass down ancient legends to attentive children.

During the late twentieth century, rapid urbanisation transformed the region. Modern roads and tech offices replaced the old fields, attracting young professionals from distant cities. People moved into contemporary high-rise flats, and busy work schedules replaced long family dinners. Many old customs began to fade away because younger generations did not use to see their practical value in everyday life.

Today, the people of Oakridge are finding creative ways to protect their cultural heritage. Every autumn, the town holds a community festival where residents celebrate both old and new ways of living. Young artists perform contemporary music alongside grandmothers who display traditional hand-woven textiles. The community shows that honoring their ancestors does not mean rejecting the benefits of modern life.

questions.question: What was Oakridge Valley like fifty years ago?
options: A quiet farming area where neighbours knew one another.
A busy metropolis with high-rise office towers.
A popular coastal holiday resort for young artists.
questions.answer: A quiet farming area where neighbours knew one another.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 states that Oakridge was a quiet farming valley where everyone knew their neighbours.

questions.question: Why does the writer use 'used to live' instead of 'would live' in the first paragraph?
options: 'Live' is a state verb, so 'would' cannot describe this past situation.
'Used to' only describes events that happen during the weekend.
'Would' is reserved exclusively for negative grammar forms.
questions.answer: 'Live' is a state verb, so 'would' cannot describe this past situation.
questions.explanation: State verbs such as 'live', 'be', and 'have' take 'used to' for past states. 'Would' cannot be used with state verbs.

questions.question: What did villagers do during summer evenings in the past?
options: They gathered near the fountain to sing folk songs and share stories.
They attended international film screenings at the town hall.
They stayed inside their private rooms to study computer science.
questions.answer: They gathered near the fountain to sing folk songs and share stories.
questions.explanation: The text says villagers would gather around the fountain to sing traditional songs and tell legends.

questions.question: What caused the landscape of Oakridge to change during the late twentieth century?
options: Rapid urbanisation and the development of modern roads and tech offices.
Severe weather conditions that destroyed all traditional farms.
A government decision to turn the whole valley into a nature park.
questions.answer: Rapid urbanisation and the development of modern roads and tech offices.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 mentions that rapid urbanisation transformed the region with new roads and tech offices replacing fields.

questions.question: What kind of housing did newer residents choose when moving to Oakridge?
options: Contemporary high-rise apartments.
Old stone houses shared with three generations.
Wooden cottages located deep inside the forest.
questions.explanation: The passage states that people moved into contemporary high-rise flats.

questions.question: Why did many ancient customs begin to fade away?
options: Younger residents did not see how these customs helped daily modern life.
The local government passed a law banning all historical rituals.
The older generation refused to speak to younger family members.
questions.answer: Younger residents did not see how these customs helped daily modern life.
questions.explanation: The text explains that customs faded because younger generations did not see their practical value in everyday life.

questions.question: What happens in Oakridge every autumn today?
options: A community festival takes place celebrating both old and modern ways of living.
All modern technology is switched off for an entire month.
Villagers build replicas of historic stone houses in the town centre.
questions.answer: A community festival takes place celebrating both old and modern ways of living.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 notes that every autumn, the town holds a festival where residents celebrate both old and new customs.

questions.question: Which detail shows how modern and traditional cultures interact at the festival?
options: Young artists play contemporary music alongside grandmothers showing woven textiles.
Farmers sell modern sports cars while teenagers wear historical armor.
Elders demand that tech companies close their offices during the festival.
questions.answer: Young artists play contemporary music alongside grandmothers showing woven textiles.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 specifically mentions young artists performing contemporary music next to grandmothers displaying hand-woven textiles.

questions.question: What is the closest meaning of 'cultural heritage' as used in Paragraph 3?
options: The customs, traditions, and arts passed down from earlier generations.
The money collected by the city council through modern taxes.
The physical machines used to produce modern computers.
questions.answer: The customs, traditions, and arts passed down from earlier generations.
questions.explanation: 'Cultural heritage' refers to the shared customs, beliefs, and artistic traditions inherited from past generations.

questions.question: What overall conclusion does the author suggest in the final sentence?
options: Honouring ancestral traditions can work side by side with modern improvements.
People must abandon all modern technology to keep their traditions alive.
Urban life completely ruins traditional values in every community.
questions.answer: Honouring ancestral traditions can work side by side with modern improvements.
questions.explanation: The closing sentence says that honoring ancestors does not mean rejecting the benefits of modern life.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Traditions in the Modern City

content.summary: Listen to two university students comparing rural cultural customs with fast modern lifestyles. Focus on past habit structures such as used to and would, and notice how weak forms sound in casual speech.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a discussion on changing cultural habits.
Identify details about past community routines and modern attitudes.
Notice how modal verbs and used to reduce in natural connected speech.

keyPhrases.note: Describes a regular past state or recurring action that no longer happens.
Expresses repeated past actions or customs in narrative storytelling.
Negative form used to contrast a past state with the present situation.
Phrasal verb describing traditions or memories slowly disappearing.

connectedSpeech.note: The 'd' merges into an unvoiced /t/ sound, and 'to' weakens to a schwa /tə/.
The modal 'would' reduces to a weak /wəd/ and links smoothly to the vowel in 'always'.
The final /t/ of didn't and the start of use link directly, followed by weak /tə/.
The /d/ in blend drops out before 'them', and 'them' reduces to /əm/.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Traditions and Changing Times

content.summary: Use used to and would to describe life in the past and compare it with life today. Use used to for past habits and past states that are no longer true. Use would for repeated past actions, but not for states. In negative sentences and questions with did, write use to without -d.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Describe Past Habits and States
blueprintItems.example: My grandmother used to live in a small village before she moved to the city.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Tell a Story About Repeated Actions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + would + base verb for repeated past actions
blueprintItems.example: Every harvest season, the villagers would gather in the town square and celebrate together.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Make Negatives and Questions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + didn't use to + base verb; Did + subject + use to + base verb?
blueprintItems.example: Did people use to wear traditional clothing every day? They didn't use to rely on technology as much as we do now.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use used to for past habits and states that are no longer true. Do not use would for a past state such as living somewhere or knowing someone.
mechanicsRules.badExample: My grandfather would live in the village before he moved.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: My grandfather used to live in the village before he moved.
mechanicsRules.why: Used to describes both past habits and past states. Would is for repeated past actions.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use would with the base verb to describe actions that happened repeatedly in the past.
mechanicsRules.badExample: During festivals, families would visited one another.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: During festivals, families would visit one another.
mechanicsRules.why: After would, use the base form of the verb, without -s or -ed.

mechanicsRules.rule: In negatives and questions with did, write use to without -d.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Did people used to travel by bus? They didn't used to have cars.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Did people use to travel by bus? They didn't use to have cars.
mechanicsRules.why: Did already marks the past, so the verb after it takes the base form.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Compare a Local Tradition with Life Today
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write four or five sentences about a local tradition. Say what people used to do, describe one repeated action with would, and compare the tradition with life today.
guidedLabChallenges.example: My grandparents used to live in a village near the river. During the New Year celebration, families would prepare food together. They would visit their neighbours in the evening. Today, many people live in the city and celebrate with relatives online.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Write about a tradition and how life has changed...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Write About a Family Memory
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write four or five sentences about a family habit from the past. Include one past state with used to, two repeated actions with would, and one question or negative sentence with use to.
guidedLabChallenges.example: My family used to live near my grandparents. Every Sunday, we would eat lunch together. My cousins would bring games to play after the meal. We didn't use to watch television during lunch. Did your family use to meet every week?
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Start writing about a family memory...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using used to. Keep the meaning the same.
practicumQuestions.promptText: In the past, my uncle lived in the countryside.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use used to for a past state.
targetAnswers: My uncle used to live in the countryside.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use used to for a past state that is no longer true. The base verb live follows used to.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence as a negative sentence using didn't use to.
practicumQuestions.promptText: People depended on mobile phones in the past.
practicumQuestions.hint: After didn't, write use to and the base verb.
targetAnswers: People didn't use to depend on mobile phones.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use didn't use to to make a negative statement about a past habit or situation. The verb depend stays in its base form.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the sentence into a question about the past.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Families used to celebrate the harvest together.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with Did and write use to without -d.
targetAnswers: Did families use to celebrate the harvest together?
practicumQuestions.explanation: In a question with did, use use to followed by the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with used to or would.
practicumQuestions.promptText: My grandmother ___ know every family in her village.
practicumQuestions.hint: Knowing people is a state, not a repeated action.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use used to for past states. Would is not normally used for states such as know.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with used to or would.
practicumQuestions.promptText: During the festival, the children ___ dance in the town square.
practicumQuestions.hint: This is an action that happened repeatedly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Would describes a repeated past action. Used to is also possible for a past habit.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the ideas with although. Keep both ideas clear.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The village is more modern now. People still celebrate the traditional festival.
targetAnswers: Although the village is more modern now, people still celebrate the traditional festival.
People still celebrate the traditional festival although the village is more modern now.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Although introduces an idea that contrasts with the main idea. Use a comma when the although clause comes first.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the ideas with because to explain the reason.
practicumQuestions.promptText: My cousins visit the old village every year. They want to learn about our family traditions.
targetAnswers: My cousins visit the old village every year because they want to learn about our family traditions.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because introduces the reason for an action. Here, the wish to learn about traditions explains the visits.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the verb form, capitalization, and punctuation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: every winter our neighbours would made a large meal
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word and use the base verb after would.
targetAnswers: Every winter, our neighbours would make a large meal.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Capitalize the first word, add a comma after the opening time phrase, and use the base verb make after would.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the question. Check the verb form, capitalization, and final punctuation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: did your parents used to wear traditional clothes
practicumQuestions.hint: After Did, write use to without -d.
targetAnswers: Did your parents use to wear traditional clothes?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Start the question with a capital letter. After did, use use to and finish the question with a question mark.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write two sentences about a tradition or family habit from the past. Use used to for a past habit or state, and would for a repeated past action.
practicumQuestions.promptText: What did people in your family or community do in the past?
practicumQuestions.hint: You may begin with People used to... and add Every year, we would...
targetAnswers: People in my family used to eat together every evening. On special days, we would prepare traditional food.
My grandparents used to live in a small town. Every summer, they would visit our family.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A good response has two complete sentences and uses the target forms correctly. Used to can describe a past habit or state, while would describes a repeated past action.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Traditions and Modern Life

content.summary: Practise comparing local traditions with contemporary urban life. Use used to for past situations and repeated habits. Use would for repeated past actions, not for past states. Give examples and explain how traditions have changed.
content.audioGuidance: Speak at a steady pace and pause briefly between your ideas. Stress the key words in each sentence, especially used to, would, and the names of customs. Let your voice fall at the end of statements. Use a rising voice when asking a yes-or-no question.

pillars.name: Clear Word Stress
pillars.target: Stress the important syllable in longer words
pillars.explanation: Say cultural with the main stress on the first syllable, and contemporary with the main stress on the second syllable. Practise each word slowly, then use it in a sentence.

pillars.name: Past Habits
pillars.target: Use used to and would accurately
pillars.explanation: Use used to for past habits and past situations, as in 'People used to live near the fields.' Use would for repeated past actions, as in 'Families would gather after the harvest.'

pillars.name: Natural Rhythm
pillars.target: Group related words into short phrases
pillars.explanation: Keep small grammar words light and make the main information clear. For example, say 'My grandmother would pass down recipes' in one smooth phrase.

pillars.name: Intonation
pillars.target: Use falling and rising tones clearly
pillars.explanation: Use a falling tone for statements and a rising tone for simple yes-or-no questions. This helps listeners understand whether you are sharing information or asking something.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Cultural has stress on its first syllable. Contemporary has stress on its second syllable.
Heritage is stressed at the beginning, while urbanisation is stressed on the fourth syllable.
In both phrasal verbs, make the first word clear and strong.
Ritual and traditional both have their main stress on the first syllable.

drills.targetText: My grandmother used to pass down traditional recipes.
drills.phonetic: /maɪ ˈɡrænmʌðə juːst tə pɑːs daʊn trəˈdɪʃənəl ˈresəpiz/
drills.focus: Link used to and stress the main content words
drills.hint: Say used to smoothly, then make pass down and recipes clear.

drills.targetText: Families would gather for a special village ritual.
drills.phonetic: /ˈfæməliz wʊd ˈɡæðə fər ə ˈspeʃəl ˈvɪlɪdʒ ˈrɪtʃuəl/
drills.hint: Keep would short and give gather and ritual a clear beat.

drills.targetText: Urbanisation has changed how people celebrate.
drills.hint: Make the fourth syllable of urbanisation the strongest.

drills.targetText: Some customs have slowly faded away.
drills.focus: Phrasal verb fade away and falling statement intonation
drills.hint: Keep faded away connected, and let your voice fall at the end.

roleplay.context: You are speaking with a classmate who is preparing a presentation about how urbanisation has affected local traditions. Share what older family members used to do and discuss which customs people still follow.

turns.speaker: Classmate
turns.text: What local traditions did your family use to follow?
turns.translation: Tradisi lokal apa yang biasa diikuti keluargamu?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: My family used to gather for a harvest meal, and my grandmother would tell us old stories.
turns.translation: Keluarga saya dulu biasa berkumpul untuk makan bersama saat panen, dan nenek saya sering menceritakan kisah-kisah lama.

turns.speaker: Classmate
turns.text: Do people still follow that tradition, or has it started to fade away?
turns.translation: Apakah orang-orang masih mengikuti tradisi itu, atau tradisi itu mulai memudar?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Some families still do it, but contemporary work and city life make it harder to meet.
turns.translation: Beberapa keluarga masih melakukannya, tetapi pekerjaan masa kini dan kehidupan kota membuat mereka lebih sulit untuk berkumpul.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a tradition you know. Describe what people did in the past and what happens now.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about a local or family tradition and how it has changed over time.
storyPoints: Describe the tradition and when people used to take part in it.
Explain what people would do and who passed the tradition down.
Say whether people still follow it today and why it may have changed.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My family used to celebrate together, and my grandparents would pass down stories about the tradition.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈfæməli juːst tə ˈselɪbreɪt təˈɡeðə ən maɪ ˈɡrænpeərənts wʊd pɑːs daʊn ˈstɔːriz əˈbaʊt ðə trəˈdɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use used to for past habits or situations and would for repeated past actions. Give at least one detail about how the tradition is different today.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds comparing a local tradition with a contemporary urban lifestyle.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: How has city life changed the way people in your community spend time together?
storyPoints: Describe how people in your community used to meet or celebrate.
Explain what people often do now in contemporary urban life.
Share one tradition people should preserve and give a reason.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: People used to meet in the village square, but now many families are busy with city life.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈpiːpəl juːst tə miːt ɪn ðə ˈvɪlɪdʒ skweə bət naʊ ˈmeni ˈfæməliz ə ˈbɪzi wɪð ˈsɪti laɪf/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make a clear comparison using past and present time phrases. Support your opinion with a simple reason.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Ask and answer questions about a family custom.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Your classmate is collecting examples of family customs for a school project. Talk about a custom in your family and how it has been passed down.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student describing a family custom. Explain what your relatives used to do and what an older family member would pass down.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Answer your classmate's questions with full sentences and add a relevant detail about the past.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Discuss an old village ritual and its purpose.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A friend is making a short audio report about village rituals. They want to know what people did before an important season and whether the ritual continues today.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are someone who has heard about a local ritual from older relatives. Describe what people would do and say whether people still do it.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describe repeated past actions with would and make clear whether the ritual still happens.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Talk about the effects of urbanisation on a local tradition.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are speaking with a community radio host who is asking how urbanisation has changed local celebrations and relationships between neighbours.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a local resident. Compare how neighbours used to celebrate with how people often spend their time now.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give one example from the past and one example of a change in the present.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Recommend a tradition that young people could help keep alive.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A youth club is planning an event about cultural heritage. The organiser wants your opinion on a tradition that could interest young people.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a youth club member. Suggest a tradition, describe how people used to practise it, and explain how young people could take part today.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make a clear suggestion and support it with a reason or a practical idea.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Use cultural heritage, pass down, contemporary, ritual, urbanisation, and fade away in spoken sentences about traditions and modern life.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Choose at least three of these words and explain how traditions have changed in your community.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Families can pass down cultural heritage, even when urbanisation changes their contemporary way of life.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈfæməliz kən pɑːs daʊn ˈkʌltʃərəl ˈherɪtɪdʒ ˈiːvən wen ˌɜːbənaɪˈzeɪʃən ˈtʃeɪndʒɪz ðeə kənˈtempərəri weɪ əv laɪf/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use the vocabulary in meaningful sentences. Pronounce each word clearly and show how it relates to a tradition or a change.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Make two spoken sentences about past habits. Use used to for a past habit or situation and would for a repeated past action.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe how people in a village used to live and one thing they would do together.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: People used to live near the fields, and they would gather for a meal after work.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈpiːpəl juːst tə lɪv nɪə ðə fiːldz ən ðeɪ wʊd ˈɡæðə fər ə miːl ˈɑːftə wɜːk/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use used to for the past situation and would for the repeated action. Do not use would to describe a past state.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say cultural heritage, contemporary, ritual, and urbanisation. Make the stressed syllable in each word easy to hear.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Repeat the four words, then say one complete sentence using any two of them.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Urbanisation has changed how people protect their cultural heritage.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˌɜːbənaɪˈzeɪʃən həz tʃeɪndʒd haʊ ˈpiːpəl prəˈtekt ðeə ˈkʌltʃərəl ˈherɪtɪdʒ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Put the main stress on the first syllable of cultural, heritage, and ritual, the second syllable of contemporary, and the fourth syllable of urbanisation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one statement with falling intonation and one yes-or-no question with rising intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: First say, 'Families would meet for a village ritual.' Then ask, 'Do families still follow this ritual?'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Families would meet for a village ritual. Do families still follow this ritual?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈfæməliz wʊd miːt fər ə ˈvɪlɪdʒ ˈrɪtʃuəl. də ˈfæməliz stɪl ˈfɒləʊ ðɪs ˈrɪtʃuəl/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice fall at the end of the statement. Let it rise at the end of the yes-or-no question.
